Let's get some historical perspective. Before 1971, tabletop game designers were either toy designers or professional military men. Arneson rocked the wargaming world with a crazy, inspired vision that was too idiosyncratic to become a product. Gygax took Arneson's idea and tamed it, chopped off some weird lumps, sanded it down and added his own obsessions. A Jew tried to get in on the ground floor but died unexpectedly before Gygax could release the first product. Arneson never truly forgave Gygax for perceived and real slights. As soon as Gygax had gotten AD&D out, his betrayers were already sharpening their knives and preparing to stab him in the back, stealing more him than he had ever stolen from Arneson.

And that was the first generation of modern tabletop gaming - D&D as practiced by TSR. They were not exactly SJWs, but they were not Aryan supermen. It's not like tabletop gaming was a glorious vanguard of artistic integrity before Gygax died. Further, it's not like D&D was an inspired vision from God - it had hundreds of major flaws even before TSR became a cocaine-fueled international banking operation. TSR had a lot of proto-SJWs and a lot of dishonorable behavior from its earliest days. As soon as TSR lost Gygax, hundreds of aspiring narcissists were trying to hustle a few bucks out of tabletop. Many of those up-and-coming narcissists were at White Wolf, and they were just as bad as today's SJWs. Tabletop gaming was never pure.
